Harper N.: Hi all — day 1 question. On an M1 Mac with the company split-tunnel VPN (WireGuard via onboarding script). I can SSH to the bastion but internal names like `api.internal.redwood` don't resolve. ping by IP works. Any quick BYOD-safe unblocks?
Ravi (infra-oncall): welcome Harper! common with split-tunnel — DNS for `*.internal` isn't routed. Quick test: `scutil --dns` ? Also which VPN client did the onboarding script install?
Harper N.: scutil shows only my home DNS. The script installed wireguard-go and created a wg0 config in /etc/wireguard. I don't want to permanently change system certs or hosts.
Maya (devex): two safe options: 1) add a systemd/dns override for the internal domain so only queries for that domain go to corp DNS, or 2) use SSH ProxyJump for git and SSH tunnels/port-forward for things like the registry. If you want DNS to work for CLI too, we can add `Domains=~internal.redwood` to a resolved conf.
Harper N.: would prefer the domain route. How do I do that on mac?
Ravi (infra-oncall): on mac create `/etc/resolver/internal.redwood` (sudo) with one line: `nameserver 10.12.2.2` and optionally `search internal.redwood`. That tells macOS to use the corporate resolver for that domain only. No global changes.
Harper N.: made the file and `scutil --dns` now shows the resolver for the domain. curl works for api.internal.redwood. But docker pull to `registry.internal:5000` still times out.
Maya (devex): registry is on a private subnet only reachable from the VPC or via bastion. Quick unblock: SSH local forward: `ssh -L 5500:registry.internal:5000 harper@bastion.redwood.internal -N` then `docker login localhost:5500` and pull. deploy-bot will log the session.
Harper N.: started the ssh forward, deploy-bot shows session open, login & pull succeeded. Thanks!
deploy-bot: (system) bastion session started for harper, audit id: f4c9e
Ravi (infra-oncall): I'll file INF-4420 to add the resolver file to the WireGuard onboarding template for BYOD so future hires get this domain resolver automatically. If you'd rather not keep the resolver file after offboarding, remove `/etc/resolver/internal.redwood`.
Harper N.: perfect. One last question — do I need to flush DNS cache after removing the resolver file?
Maya (devex): on mac run `sudo dscacheutil -flushcache; sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder` after removing the file to clear cached entries.
Harper N.: awesome, everything's unblocked. Thanks for the quick help! :tada:
